# incident_access_group (Resource)

Manage access groups: named groups of users that access grants give privileges to. Membership is managed in the dashboard or through SCIM.

This resource manages custom access groups. Who belongs to a group is not managed here: add people in the dashboard, or map the group to a group in your identity provider with SCIM. Give a group privileges with `incident_access_grant`.

Every organization also has the base groups `owner`, `admin` and `standard`, which cannot be renamed or deleted. Look those up with the `incident_access_group` data source instead of managing them here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom access group. Add people to it in the dashboard, or map it to a group in your
# identity provider with SCIM: Terraform manages the group, not who is in it.
resource "incident_access_group" "platform" {
  name        = "Platform engineers"
  description = "Engineers who own our on-call and catalog setup"
}

# Give the group privileges with an access grant.
resource "incident_access_grant" "platform" {
  principal = {
    type = "access_group"
    id   = incident_access_group.platform.id
  }
  resource = {
    type = "organization"
  }
  privileges = [
    "catalog_types.create",
    "schedules.create",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable name, unique within the organisation

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description of who belongs in this group
- `slug` (String) Stable identifier, unique within the organisation. Base groups use owner, admin and standard. Generated from the name when omitted on create, and cannot be changed later. Changing it replaces the group.
- `unlock_in_dashboard` (Boolean) Whether to leave this resource unlocked in the incident.io dashboard, so people can edit it there. Defaults to `false`: Terraform claims what it manages, and a claimed resource cannot be edited in the dashboard. Set it to `true` to leave the resource unclaimed — pair that with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [...] }` naming the attributes people edit, or the next apply reverts them. Setting it on a resource Terraform already claimed hands that resource back, and someone disconnecting one in the dashboard shows as no change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this access group
- `type` (String) base for the groups every organisation has, which cannot be changed or deleted, or custom for groups you create

## Import

Import is supported using an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) or the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import):

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash

# Import an access group using its ID
# Replace the ID with a real ID from your incident.io organization
terraform import incident_access_group.example 01ABC123DEF456GHI789JKL
```
